FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A35
A person's physical condition and emotional state can influence driving performance. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A35
The handbook connects safe driving with full attention and control of emotions. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A35
Forward vision helps a driver recognize important objects and respond to them. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A35
Peripheral vision helps a driver notice objects approaching from either side. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A35
Judging distance is one of the visual abilities needed for sound driving decisions. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A35
Sounds such as horns, sirens and nearby vehicles can help a driver make safer decisions. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A35
The handbook advises drivers with hearing loss to use hearing aids when possible or compensate through stronger visual observation. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A35
The handbook advises consulting a physician when illness or disability may affect the ability to drive safely. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A35
An applicant reporting a seizure or loss of consciousness during the three months before obtaining or renewing an operator license is asked for a physician's safe-driving certification. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A35
The handbook recommends regular vision examinations for people with diabetes. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A35
The handbook advises physician consultation before driving for people with heart disease, high blood pressure or circulation problems. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A35
Diabetes, a heart condition or another medical condition causing loss of consciousness in the three months before operator-license issuance or renewal triggers a physician's safe-driving certification requirement. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A35
The handbook advises asking a physician or pharmacist how a prescription medicine could affect driving. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A35
Review nonprescription medicine packaging for side effects that could impair driving. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A35
The handbook prohibits nitrous oxide use in a motor vehicle being operated on a Nebraska public roadway. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A35
The handbook describes reasonable suspicion of a traffic or criminal violation as the basis for an officer's traffic stop. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A35
When emergency lights appear behind the vehicle, the driver and passengers are advised to remain calm and cooperate. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A35
Signal and move off the road or to its side at the first safe opportunity when being stopped. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A36
During the stop, switch off the engine and audio equipment. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A36
Remain inside the vehicle unless the officer directs you to get out. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A36
If stopped at night, illuminate the vehicle's interior so the officer can see inside. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A36
An officer may use a spotlight to improve visibility during a stop. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A36
Keep your hands on the wheel or another place where the officer can readily see them. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A36
Follow the instructions the officer gives to you and your passengers. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

Misconceptions: Signing a traffic ticket is different from admitting guilt; a request for documents is different from permission to reach for them.
Mnemonics: Signal, stop safely, stay visible, wait for directions.
Glossary: Financial responsibility is the handbook's required insurance protection; certification is a physician's statement about safe vehicle operation.
Dynamic facts: Live contact details, services and variable fees are withheld from this stable inventory.
